queue.title: Democrats’ midterm sweep opens path to bypassing Electoral College by 2028
queue.dek: Democrat trifectas in key swing states could push the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact past 270 electoral votes needed to activate it and thus change the way Americans select the presidency.
queue.opening: Democrats’ midterm gains have opened a new front in the fight over how America chooses its president — one that could reshape the 2028 race for the White House. Democrats now control the governor’s office and both chambers of the state legislature in Michigan, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin and Nevada. The National Popular Vote Interstate Compact, already enacted by 18 states and Washington, D.C., has 222 electoral votes pledged to it — 48 short of the 270 needed to take effect. If the four states join, their combined 50 electoral votes would push the compact to 272 and activate it. Arizona could push the total to 283 if Democrats ultimately gain control of both chambers there. National Popular Vote (NPV), the nonprofit organization that authored the compact and is campaigning to enact it state by state, says it has identified multiple legislative sponsors in each of the five states whose combined electoral votes could push the compact over the 270-vote threshold. It expects bills to be pre-filed before, or introduced early, in the 2027 legislative sessions. "I am confident we have multiple paths to secure the 48 electoral votes required to deliver what 63% of Americans want," Patrick Rosenstiel, a senior consultant for NPV, told Fox News Digital. queue.title: New Jersey town reveals staggering $26M theft days after election, sparking backlash
queue.dek: Cranbury Township residents demand answers after a $26 million fraudulent wire transfer was kept secret until days after Election Day in New Jersey.
queue.opening: A New Jersey township is facing backlash after officials revealed that $26 million was stolen in a fraudulent wire transfer, with residents questioning why the massive theft wasn't disclosed until more than five weeks later — just days after Election Day. Cranbury Township Mayor Lisa Knierim announced Friday that the municipality had been the victim of a "sophisticated financial theft" involving approximately $26 million. Knierim, a Democrat, said the fraudulent wire transfer took place on Sept. 28, with the funds originally designated for purchasing property to meet the township's affordable housing obligations. A task force involving local, county, state and federal law enforcement agencies, led by the township's police department and the Middlesex County Prosecutor's Office, is working to recover the funds, according to the mayor's statement. CYBERCRIME LOSSES NEAR $21B: 5 WAYS TO PROTECT YOUR MONEY So far, investigators have frozen nearly $17.3 million in assets, leaving approximately $8.7 million outside the reported freeze. The township said the investigation remains active, adding that additional details cannot be released. Knierim's announcement came Nov. 6, three days after the midterm elections and more than five weeks after the theft. Several residents responded to the announcement on the township's Facebook page, questioning the timing of the disclosure and demanding greater transparency from local officials. Herzog announced his decision on Nov. 7, but the formal presentation of the mandate is scheduled for Sunday, Nov. 8, at 5 p.m. Israeli time. Eisenkot will then have 28 days to assemble a government, with a possible 14-day extension. The decision could mark a significant step toward ending Netanyahu’s tenure, but it would also launch a difficult round of coalition negotiations, with deep disagreements among parties seeking to replace him. queue.opening: A Biden-appointed federal judge ordered ICE's Denver field office director to appear in court Monday amid concerns that immigration authorities violated judicial release orders by immediately rearresting detainees, including at least one instance outside a detention center. Nathan Rasper has been summoned as part of an inquiry involving 14 people who were arrested after being released from immigration detention . The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) maintains that ICE complied with lawful court orders and that a judicial release order does not permanently shield individuals from immigration enforcement. "When an illegal alien is ordered released by a judge, that does not immunize the alien from immigration enforcement for all time," DHS said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "ICE may seek to rearrest the alien in a way that complies with the judicial decision. To suggest that ICE cannot do this is nothing short of sabotage." queue.dek: The IRS released its 2027 tax brackets with a boost to the standard deduction and a $100 increase to the child tax credit for families.
queue.opening: The IRS recently released updated tax brackets and deduction thresholds for the 2027 tax year, which will affect taxpayers next year. Each year, the IRS adjusts the thresholds used for tax brackets and the various deductions available to taxpayers to account for inflation. The changes will apply to what taxpayers owe on income earned during the 2027 tax year, which Americans will file returns for in 2028. "American individuals and businesses will see increased tax benefits next tax year ranging from an increase in the standard deduction and the Child Tax Credit for families, and a boost to the amount that can be expensed by businesses," said IRS CEO Frank Bisignano. The standard deduction , claimed by the majority of taxpayers who don't itemize their returns, is set to increase to $16,600 for single taxpayers in 2027; $33,200 for married couples filing jointly and $24,925 for heads of households.
